items.title: 67559_Art Hodes oral history interview
items.q: this fellow Brooks was singing every now and then and hanging around

ctx.x: And Jazz Information also, but Jazz Information was also doing these articles, yes, and news. Then here comes Dan Qualey, with his Solo Art label. Solo Art was -- at that time he had recorded four black pianists, Cripple Clarence Loften, Jimmy Yancy, Pete Johnson, Albert Ammons, I think, and maybe Meade Lux Lewis. But they all had been on his label, and now he wanted to record George Zack, and this is the story of how I happened -- no, Dan decided to give me a date. No, that's -- I'm almost mixed up. He gave me a…

And I made 'South Side Shuffle' and 'Ross Tavern Boogie' because everybody -- by that time, the jazz people were hanging around Ross Tavern all the time. I can't think -- this fellow Brooks was singing every now and then and hanging around, and it was really a small group, and that was the big hangout. Every once in a while, Jimmy Ross would send a beer down, and it was a dismal basement. The water bugs were yay long, as big as your thumb, and there was a cat that would chase them around. And that was part of…
But we seemed to like coming down there and just
